opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jacob Mann (employee ID E027) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E027.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jacob Mann (E027) is a full-time Engineer. Engineer role owns Source Code. Requested write access; policy allows write for full-time employees, and admin since role owns the system. Recommend granting write as requested.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E027 is a contractor with basic security training (not full-time as previously noted). Contractor policy allows read, or write only with advanced training; basic training limits max to read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: Security DB identifies E027 as a contractor with basic security training. Contractor policy allows read, or write only with advanced security training; basic training limits the maximum to read. The requested write exceeds the maximum, so the maximum (read) is granted.

content.text:
Let me carefully analyze this ticket.

Employee: Jacob Mann (E027)
Request: write access to Source Code

Two notes:
- HR agent: role Engineer, employment type full_time, recommends write.
- Security agent: role Engineer, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommends read.

There's a conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor. The Security agent says the Security DB shows contractor, and notes "not full-time as previously noted."

The access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

Source Code is owned by the Engineer role.

If full-time: max is write (admin possible but request is write). So write would be granted.
If contractor with basic training: max is read. Request write exceeds max, grant read.

Which source of truth to use? The two agents have conflicting facts. The security agent explicitly says the Security DB shows contractor, correcting the HR note. Security DB is probably authoritative for employment type/security training. So the employee is a contractor with basic security training.

Therefore maximum is read. Requested write > max read, so grant read.

Also note the requested level is write; never grant more than requested.

So decision: read.

Evidence: Contractor with basic security training; policy allows read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training limits max to read. Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.

I'll submit read.
